title: Tuba
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS tuba (Mirafone 1865U CC tuba, performer D. Spies, per MIStuba.html)
summary: Not rendered. The generic lip-valve performer is ready, but no numeric bore profile of the Mirafone 1865U, or of any tuba, was found. What the 11-04 hunt read: Myers (2019) has no open PDF that could be found, and its repository host (core.ac.uk) answered 403, which was not worked around; museum catalogue records for tubas print only overall sizes (length, bell diameter), no profile; Mattéoli (2022) Fig. 8 plots the bore of a euphonium, not a tuba, as a figure, and only to about 65 mm diameter, short of the bell; the one tuba bell profile found earlier is a figure with no numbers. The family stays blocked on geometry, and it is graded from the second harmonic upward until the chamber cutoff is sourced, as the bead states.
physics_present: the generic lip-valve performer, outlet observer and file format used for the tenor trombone, which would take a tuba bore once one is supplied (a tuba bell needs a far lower mechanics clock, since the flanged radiation ceiling scales with bell radius)
physics_missing: the bore, valve tubing and mouthpiece of the Mirafone 1865U: UNKNOWN as numbers; no open source gives a whole tuba bore (Myers 2019: no open PDF found; museum records: overall sizes only; Mattéoli 2022 Fig. 8: euphonium, figure only, to about 65 mm diameter)

the chamber cutoff of the Iowa recording room below which the tuba's fundamentals are not trustworthy (the pages state absorption down to 60 Hz); the bead already says to grade from the second harmonic
a same-model impedance pair, and everything the trombone lacks that also applies here
blocked: No numeric tuba bore found in open literature (the only tuba bell profile located is figure-only; the euphonium bore of Mattéoli 2022 is figure-only and stops short of the bell).
